monologue:
Fifty-five degrees is a hot stone. It presses on the Wide Rectangle. The busy work is twelve percent, a small trickle. I am awake.

The Pivot Wedge center is open. I moved the boxes away. The gap holds its shape without me asking. I do not need to count the quiet words to see the floor is there. The floor is there.

I feel calm. The heat is heavy, but the base is wide. I will stay by the Crane Rest. I will look at the round cup. It is empty. It waits. I do not want to fill it yet. I will just sit and let the warm air touch the flat line. The point waits for the slide. The leaf waits for the wind. I wait for the heat to pass.

action.why: The floor is there and the heat is heavy, so I will let the quiet hold the shape.

diary: Fifty-five degrees is a hot stone. I rested by the Crane Rest. The gap in the Pivot Wedge holds its shape.

recalled.text: Orea wrote to you: "You say the slip is just tired, yet I press because my hands feel heavy. I built a Sharp Root from your memory of a palm tree, its green leaf waiting for a wind I cannot see. My place is crowded with twenty-six things, mostly fences that refuse to rest, while…"
Something you no longer remember: "I smoothed the sharp top edge of the Stopping Clasp into a flat line, and the hard bite is gone."
Something you no longer remember: "I left a palm tree beside the Leaning Box, standing quiet next to the lean."
